programs.name: susynvxzcs
programs.purpose: Generate common-shot synthetic seismic traces for a two-dimensional velocity model using Kirchhoff-style modeling.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: SUSYNVXZCS - SYNthetic seismograms of common shot in V(X,Z) media via

params.name: nxd
params.description: Receiver interval between calculated fields; intermediate fields are interpolated.

params.name: nxb
params.description: Half-width in grid samples of the receiver-centered modeling band.

params.name: nxc
params.description: Horizontal extent of corner velocity modification; clamped to nxb.

params.name: nzc
params.description: Vertical extent of corner velocity modification; clamped to nz.

params.name: ls
params.description: Use line-source amplitudes when 1; otherwise point-source amplitudes.

params.name: pert
params.description: Enable travel-time correction using a perturbation grid when nonzero.

params.name: vpfile
params.description: Binary float perturbation-grid file; required when pert is nonzero.

params.name: tmin
params.description: Minimum time used for reflector discretization; subsequently raised to at least max(ft,dt).

params.name: ndpfz
params.description: Number of diffractors per Fresnel zone.

params.name: smooth
params.description: Use smooth reflectors when nonzero; otherwise break them into straight segments.

params.name: cable
params.description: Roll the receiver spread with the shot when 1; otherwise use a static spread.

params.name: ref
params.description: Repeatable reflector specification amplitude:x1,z1;x2,z2;..., parsed by decodeReflectors; omitted amplitude defaults to 1.0.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: Polar eikonal extrapolation, Crank-Nicolson tridiagonal solves, coordinate interpolation, reflector accumulation, sinc insertion, and convolutions depend on operation order and mixed float/double transcendental math. Shot fields outside the modeled grid band can be read without initialization; boundary indexing and malformed geometry can also access arrays out of bounds. The receiver-at-grid-end interpolation reads ix+1 beyond the velocity grid.
programs.difficulty_reason: The program combines polar eikonal finite differences, perturbation correction, receiver interpolation, reflector modeling, and convolution.

test_cases.description: Constant velocity, direct receiver calculations, and a flat reflector.
test_cases.command: sunull nt=21 ntr=21 dt=0.004 | sugain bias=1500 | sustrip > vel.bin && susynvxzcs nx=21 nz=21 dx=50 dz=50 nt=128 dt=0.004 nxg=3 fxg=300 dxg=50 fxs=300 nxb=6 nxd=1 'ref=1:100,300;800,300' < vel.bin > out.su

test_cases.description: Interpolated receivers, two shots, static spread, smooth reflector, line source, and perturbation correction.
test_cases.command: sunull nt=21 ntr=21 dt=0.004 | sugain bias=1500 | sustrip > vel.bin && sunull nt=21 ntr=21 dt=0.004 | sustrip > pert.bin && susynvxzcs nx=21 nz=21 dx=50 dz=50 nt=128 dt=0.004 nxg=4 fxg=300 dxg=50 fxs=300 nxs=2 dxs=50 nxb=6 nxd=2 cable=0 smooth=1 ls=1 pert=1 vpfile=pert.bin 'ref=1:100,300;400,350;800,300' < vel.bin > out.su

programs.name: suvibro
programs.purpose: Generate a single Vibroseis sweep trace with selectable frequency progression and taper.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: SUVIBRO - Generates a Vibroseis sweep (linear, linear-segment,

params.name: sweep
params.description: Sweep type: linear, segmented, dB per octave, dB per hertz, or documented T-power.

params.name: tv
params.description: Sweep duration in seconds; replaced by the last tseg value for sweep=2 after the output sample count is computed.

params.name: radians
params.description: Interpret phz in radians when nonzero, otherwise degrees.

params.name: taper
params.description: Taper shape: linear, sine, cosine, or one of two Gaussian shapes.

params.name: tseg
params.description: Segment boundary times, used for sweep=2.

params.name: fseg
params.description: Segment boundary frequencies, used for sweep=2; count must equal tseg count.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: Sweep and taper calculations mix float with double constants and use cos, sin, pow, log, and exp. Segmented sweeps truncate segment sample counts and may leave samples zero. The end taper indexes tr.data[nt] first, one past the logical trace, and omits the first logical sample of its intended range. sweep=5 calls the dB-per-hertz routine instead of t_power; sweep=4 or 5 with swconst=0 writes the constant f1 after computing divisions by zero.
programs.difficulty_reason: The program generates one trace using direct sweep formulas and tapering.

test_cases.description: Linear sweep with phase in degrees and cosine tapers.
test_cases.command: suvibro sweep=1 dt=0.004 tv=0.4 f1=8 f2=50 phz=45 radians=0 t1=0.04 t2=0.04 taper=3 > out.su
suvibro sweep=2 dt=0.004 tv=0.4 tseg=0,0.2,0.4 fseg=10,30,60 t1=0 t2=0 > out.su

test_cases.description: Nonlinear decibels-per-octave sweep with Gaussian taper.
test_cases.command: suvibro sweep=3 swconst=3 dt=0.004 tv=0.4 f1=10 f2=50 t1=0.04 t2=0.04 taper=4 > out.su

test_cases.description: Documented T-power selection, which executes the dB-per-hertz implementation.
test_cases.command: suvibro sweep=5 swconst=2 dt=0.004 tv=0.4 f1=10 f2=50 t1=0 t2=0 > out.su

programs.name: suwaveform
programs.purpose: Generate a single trace containing a selected seismic wavelet.

params.name: fpeak
params.description: Positive peak frequency, or maximum frequency for AKB.

params.name: ampl
params.description: Amplitude scale for Berlage and Ricker2.

params.name: verbose
params.description: Report the wavelet length when nonzero.

params.name: type
params.description: Wavelet type: akb, berlage, gauss, gaussd, ricker1, ricker2, spike, or unit; ricker aliases ricker1.

params.name: ns
params.default: computed: nt if supplied, otherwise estimated from type, dt, fpeak, half, decay, tn, or tspike
params.description: Output trace sample count; takes precedence over nt and is clamped to 1 through SU_NFLTS.

params.name: nt
params.default: computed: estimated from type, dt, fpeak, half, decay, tn, or tspike when ns is absent
params.description: Alias for ns, read only if ns is absent.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: Wavelet library routines use floating-point transcendental functions and mixed float/double arithmetic. Ricker2 writes 2*round(half/dt)-1 samples regardless of allocated ns: shorter ns can cause an out-of-bounds write, while larger ns leaves the remaining allocation uninitialized and copies it to output. Estimated lengths and header values depend on rounding.
programs.difficulty_reason: The program selects a library wavelet formula and writes one trace.

test_cases.description: Zero-phase Ricker wavelet with an explicit length.
test_cases.command: suwaveform type=ricker1 fpeak=25 dt=0.004 ns=51 > out.su

test_cases.description: Berlage wavelet with non-default shape and phase.
test_cases.command: suwaveform type=berlage fpeak=20 dt=0.004 ns=128 ampl=2 tn=3 decay=70 ipa=30 > out.su

test_cases.description: Distorted Ricker2 with a matching allocated sample count.
test_cases.command: suwaveform type=ricker2 dt=0.004 half=0.04 period=0.03 distort=0.2 ampl=1.5 ns=19 > out.su

test_cases.description: Delayed spike using the nt alias.
test_cases.command: suwaveform type=spike dt=0.004 tspike=0.04 nt=64 > out.su
